features.feature: Every Finding-system mutation is durable and has application-level exactly-once effect under the supported writer model.
Executed mutable runtime artifacts are cryptographically bound to source material and command before later consumption.
Story 3 owns P6 and the runtime half of P4, only mitigates persistence/runtime portions of P1, and makes no claim to reduce genuine repair work.
Audit and reuse per-Story, main/B-META, process-event, build, and Store transaction primitives instead of creating an uncoordinated lock tree.
Deliver one Story in internal order 3A ledger integrity before 3B runtime integrity, with later authority unable to bypass that order.

The shared transaction primitive supports Finding, candidate-route, assessment-proposal/final-assessment, mandatory-repair, expiry-policy, deferral, supersession, route, baseline-set, material re-attestation, manifest, and receipt records.
A schema-neutral fenced transaction can append a standalone record or compare exact referenced bytes/current-chain state and atomically commit multiple records without interpreting their semantics.
Record IDs are collision-resistant, append-only, and independent of mutable array length.
Idempotency-key replay returns the original semantic and receipt IDs with zero additional rows.
Exact-record CAS binds expected record IDs/hashes, observed chain head, predicate digest, and prior ledger digest; every mismatch writes zero semantic rows.
Successful local-FS publication completes temp write, file fsync, atomic rename, directory fsync, and installed-digest verification before success is returned.
Crash/kill/partial-temp recovery is deterministic and a successor fence prevents a paused stale writer from publishing rows or receipts.
Unsupported multi-host/NFS, corruption, stale epoch, or insufficient writer capability assumptions fail closed before semantic mutation.
Canonical Story/B-META lock roots compose with Finding, process-event, and build writers without nested-lock deadlock.
One hundred concurrent unique Finding appends produce exactly 100 unique durable rows.
Concurrent/replayed/crashed legacy identity first reads converge on one immutable tuple/hash and record ID without rewriting legacy Finding bytes.
Concurrent mixed record-type transactions lose no rows and preserve all record references, including material re-attestations.
FindingLedgerReceipt carries and signs the complete accepted epoch, capability, operation, CAS, digest, replay, fence, trust, hash, and signature contract and never recursively receipts itself.

append_assessment_proposal atomically persists one immutable exact-union proposal plus one receipt, and its shared verifier rejects wrong authority/signature, altered union, missing lookup, stale/expired proposal, and proposal/final divergence.
Mandatory-repair classify/close and expiry-policy records are append-only, unique, idempotent, and never half-visible with referenced manifests.
Standalone receipt and initial receipt-plus-four-baseline bundles are complete-or-absent, exact-byte receipted, idempotent, and retain signed non-gate authority markers.
A later CandidateRoute CAS can consume an exact standalone receipt while any conflict leaves the receipt byte-identical and writes no route.
A later Story 1 exact receipt/baseline CAS can atomically commit deferral plus manifest/action or neither, with idempotent same-ID retry.
Concurrent revoke/supersede versus apply has a deterministic serialized winner and no commit can bind a non-latest receipt.
RuntimeEvidenceReceipt has a production signer/verifier and build/execution adapter, not merely a test helper.
Real registered finding_runtime_evidence_run and finding_runtime_evidence_verify CLI handlers execute, persist, reload, and verify through the production adapter.

Runtime receipts bind source HEAD/material, build policy/command, execution command, outputs, allowlisted/redacted environment, artifact manifest, toolchain, producer, key, algorithm, trust root, and freshness policy through immutable content-addressed blobs.
Build-in-progress is refused and artifact identity/digest/realpath/build state must remain stable before, during, and after execution.
Runtime verification rejects source/command/environment/toolchain/output/artifact/trust/blob/signature/realpath/TOCTOU tamper with deterministic reason codes and leaks no secrets or protected paths.
append_runtime_receipt uses the Story 3 ledger exactly once: replay and crash/retry return original runtime-record and ledger-receipt IDs without half-visible or duplicate rows.
Process facts distinguish atomic persistence authority from gate-eligible runtime evidence and never promote stored candidate/route/baseline/history/receipt bytes into semantic lifecycle authority.
finding_ledger_query exposes signed deterministic complete ledger/CAS/idempotency/runtime-scorecard/migration inputs with no protected storage paths.
Registry, command-policy, phase-allowlist, direct-consumer, authority-marker, incomplete-row, and path-leakage mutations fail mechanically.
Story 3 builds with no import from Story 2 or Story 1, while 3B may consume only 3A schema-neutral APIs.
The actual Story dependency DAG is enforced: B-03b7 depends on B-fe8f and B-e6d9 depends on both B-fe8f and B-03b7; failed early advances write no transition.
Public query scorecard inputs are deterministic, complete, signed, reject tamper/incompleteness, and are consumed without protected-storage parsing.
RED first audits current primitives, preserves already-correct behavior, and creates failures only for genuine current contract gaps rather than replaying an assumed historical race.
Every genuine RED is recorded through official red_evidence_create and a digest-bound immutable red_green_relation that proves pre-fix failure and later unchanged-assertion GREEN.
The RED commit modifies no production files and contains only the executable characterization artifact plus CLI-owned evidence.
Final GREEN covers concurrency, CAS, runtime, tamper, registry, query, dependency, rollback, migration, and preserves characterized existing behavior without weakening RED.
Rollback/kill-switch and schema-epoch migration preserve committed readable history, reject unsupported epochs, and cause no data loss or legacy byte rewrite.

Because this Story changes CLI/runtime behavior, patch version increments exactly once across root package, main package, lockfile, packages/main/src/core/lattice-brand.ts LATTICE_CLI_VERSION, local CLI, and installed CLI.
Detector classification and detector precision implementation are outside Story 3.
